statements.t: We record income from MSRs at the time of commitment to the borrower, which represents the fair value of the expected net future cash flows associated with the rights to service mortgage loans that we originate, with the recognition of a corresponding asset upon sale.

However, depending on market conditions and asset-specific factors, we may evaluate other alternatives, such as recapitalizations and joint venture structures, intended to optimize recoveries and reduce our REO exposure.
However, given the current interest rate environment and inflationary pressures, we cannot assure that our loan portfolio will continue to perform in accordance with current contractual terms.

The overall reductions in short-term interest rates have reduced, and are expected to continue to reduce, net interest income on our floating rate loan portfolio and earnings on our cash and escrow balances.
Based on our evaluation to date, we expect certain changes under the OBBBA, including changes affecting the application of Section 162(m), to increase our current tax expense and effective tax rate.

Because implementation of these tax and other provisions remains subject to further interpretation and guidance, the ultimate impact on our business, financial condition, results of operations and the real estate markets in general could differ from our current expectations.

The timing and amounts of these sources depend on market conditions, asset performance and execution of planned transactions, and there can be no assurance that projected liquidity will be adequate to meet our liquidity needs.

We expect to seek additional liquidity through loan repayments, sales of loans, dispositions of REO assets, improved utilization of existing financing arrangements, and capital retention through dividend suspension.
Accordingly, we may experience delays in converting certain legacy loans and REO assets into cash, and the proceeds ultimately realized may be lower than previously anticipated.
While we expect to extend or renew all of our facilities as they mature, we cannot provide assurance that they will be extended or renewed on as favorable terms.

Distributable earnings is not intended to be an indication of our cash flows from operating activities (determined in accordance with GAAP) or a measure of our liquidity, nor is it entirely indicative of funding our cash needs, including our ability to make cash distributions.

The Company will continue to evaluate its dividend policy based upon market conditions and the Company's performance, capital needs, and REIT distribution requirements with a continued focus on preserving book value and maximizing long-term shareholder value.
